level_id_bank.verdict: NOT HELD. EXCLUDE at the print -- but this is the most interesting EXCLUDE in either batch, because the thing to do is defined and simply not yet triggered. Price 1,175.1 sits 1.3% BELOW the gate (C 3.618 = 1,190.0, and the operator drew a cyan line at 1,192.2 -- the only line they drew on the whole drop), with the nearest real support 7.7% down (the three-ladder olive band 1,057.5-1,084.4) and the verified floor 16% down. Trend is DOWN on both the weekly and the monthly: price is under a falling 1W SMA50 (1,363.3) and a rolling-over 1W EMA200 (1,453.5), and the monthly stack is inverted. So this is a bounce inside a downtrend, not a trend. R:R at the print is 0.41. TWO WAYS TO PLAY IT, neither of which is a buy here. (1) THE RECLAIM, and it is the better one: a WEEKLY close above 1,192.2 would be the first structure reclaimed in the entire 2026 decline, and above it there is a genuinely thin stretch -- two lone rungs (1,225.9 and 1,294.4) with no MA, band or volume node until the 1,363-1,434 wall. Entry on the weekly close above 1,192.2, stop on a weekly close back below 1,148.3 (D 1.886), first target 1,225.9, then 1,294.4, then the wall base 1,363.3: from ~1,195 that is 3.9% of risk for a 14.1% run to the wall = R:R 3.6. (2) THE RETEST of 971.97-988.4, the five-source floor that ALREADY worked -- the 2026 low printed 982.40 there and closed 985.30, 0.09% from a surpassed ladder's rung, and price is +19.3% off it. If it is ever offered again with the weekly RSI still above its average, that is the highest-quality entry on the chart. What kills both: a weekly close below 1,057.5 loses the three-ladder band and puts the floor back in play from above.
